topic: Modern C++ Range-based Algorithms and Iterators
explanation: In modern C++, range-based algorithms from the Standard Template Library (STL) provide powerful, expressive, and efficient ways to operate on collections of data. These algorithms, such as for_each(), copy(), transform(), and merge(), work seamlessly with iterators and support generic programming. They enable developers to write concise, safe, and high-performance code by abstracting common iteration patterns, often leveraging modern C++ features like auto, lambda expressions, and move semantics. Understanding how to utilize these algorithms is essential for writing idiomatic C++ that is both readable and efficient.
